title_en: How Your Eye Forms an Image
text_en: Light enters through the pupil. The lens focuses the light onto the retina, where cells detect the image.
text_zh: 光从瞳孔进入眼睛，再由晶状体聚焦到视网膜。视网膜上的感光细胞把这些光变成我们看到的图像。

title_en: Why Some Objects Are Hard to See
title_zh: 为什么有些天体肉眼难以看见
text_en: Your eyes collect only a small amount of light. Bright objects like the Moon are easy to see, but faint galaxies need a telescope.
text_zh: 眼睛的集光能力有限。月球够亮，肉眼就能看见；暗淡的星系通常要靠望远镜多收一些光。

text_en: After early-1600s spyglasses appeared, Galileo improved a telescope and used it astronomically; he did not invent it. The objective lens forms an image and the eyepiece magnifies it, so maria and crater rims can be compared with the naked-eye Moon.
text_zh: 17 世纪初，伽利略改进望远镜并把它用于观星，但他并不是望远镜的发明者。物镜先成像，目镜再放大，月海和环形山边缘就能从模糊斑块变成可辨认的结构。

text_en: Most sky objects are so far away that their light reaches the telescope almost parallel. The focus knob moves the eyepiece until the image formed at the focal plane looks sharp.
text_zh: 多数天体距离非常远，进入望远镜的光几乎是平行的。调焦旋钮会移动目镜位置，让焦平面上的图像变清楚。

text_en: Higher magnification makes objects look larger, but it also narrows the view and can make the image dimmer or shakier.
text_zh: 更高倍率会让目标看起来更大，但也会让视野变窄，并可能让图像更暗、更抖。

text_en: A finder scope shows a wider field than the main telescope, because more magnification also makes navigation harder. Align both tubes, then use the real observing rhythm: Eye to Finder to Main Scope. Even experienced observers rely on it.
text_zh: 主望远镜倍率高、视野窄，不适合直接找目标。先把寻星镜和主镜校到同一方向，再按肉眼、寻星镜、主镜的顺序观测，老手也会这么做。

title_en: Why the Refractor Shows Colored Fringes
title_zh: 折射镜为什么出现彩色边缘
text_en: A simple objective lens bends blue light more strongly than red light, so the colors reach focus at slightly different positions. Even when the star looks sharp, red and blue fringes can remain. A reflector uses mirrors instead of a large objective lens, so it avoids this lens chromatic aberration.
text_zh: 简单物镜对蓝光和红光的弯折程度不同，两种颜色会落在稍有差异的焦点上。所以星点已经清楚时，边缘仍可能留下红蓝彩边。反射镜不用大型物镜，也就避开了这类透镜色差。

title_zh: 牛顿反射望远镜如何工作
text_en: A refractor can keep colored fringes even at best focus. Isaac Newton built a practical reflector to avoid this lens color separation. Its curved primary gathers light, a diagonal secondary sends it to the side focuser, and collimation keeps both mirrors on one optical axis.
text_zh: 折射镜即使在最佳焦点也可能保留彩边。艾萨克·牛顿制造了实用反射望远镜，以避开这种透镜颜色分离。弯曲主镜负责集光，斜副镜把光送向侧置调焦器，而准直让两面镜子保持在同一光轴上。

text_en: A larger aperture collects more light. This helps faint objects like nebulae and galaxies become easier to see.
text_zh: 更大的口径可以收集更多光，让星云和星系这类暗目标更容易被看见。

text_en: Deep-sky objects are faint. A stable telescope, large aperture, and suitable low magnification are more useful than simply increasing power.
text_zh: 深空天体很暗。稳定的望远镜、大口径和合适的低倍率，比单纯提高倍率更有用。

text_en: A reflector only works when its mirrors line up. Collimation tilts the mirrors until light converges exactly at the eyepiece.
text_zh: 反射望远镜的镜子必须对齐才能成像。准直就是微调镜子的角度，让光线恰好汇聚到目镜位置。

title_zh: 视宁度：星星为什么会晃
text_en: Warm, moving air bends starlight randomly, like looking through the shimmer above a campfire. Calm air keeps a star's light steady; turbulent air makes it blur and dance. Low targets near the horizon suffer most, since their light passes through much more of that thick, unsteady air.
text_zh: 流动的暖空气会不断弯折星光，就像隔着热浪看东西。大气平稳时星点很安静；湍流强时会模糊、跳动。目标越靠近地平线，光穿过的大气越厚，影响也越明显。

title_en: Light Pollution: The Sky's Background Light
text_en: City lights brighten the whole sky, like leaving every lamp on while hunting fireflies in a room. Faint objects like Andromeda are still there, but the bright background hides most of their light. A darker sky reveals far more stars and lets faint galaxies stand out clearly.
text_zh: 城市灯光会抬高整片夜空的亮度，像在开着灯的房间里找微弱光点。仙女座仍在那里，只是外围被明亮背景吞掉了。换到更暗的天空，星系的淡结构才会重新显出来。

title_en: Cloud Gaps: A Real Observing Skill
text_en: Thin clouds drift across the sky and dim your target as they pass. Waiting for a gap between clouds is not a failure - it's a real skill every observer uses. Half of observing is watching the sky, and the other half is watching the clouds.
text_zh: 薄云经过目标时，亮度会暂时下降。这时候保持居中，别拿调焦去追云层造成的变暗。等云隙出现再观测，是很普通也很重要的耐心活。

text_en: Your eyes slowly become more sensitive in the dark - full dark adaptation takes about 20-30 minutes, as color-sensing cone cells hand off to more light-sensitive rod cells. Once adapted, try averted vision: look slightly to the side of a faint object instead of straight at it. This lets its light land on the rod-rich periphery of your retina, where faint glows are easier to detect.
text_zh: 眼睛会在黑暗中逐渐变得敏感，充分暗适应通常需要 20-30 分钟。看暗弱天体时，可以让视线偏到目标旁边一点，让光落在杆细胞更密集的视网膜周边，淡光反而更容易被察觉。

text_en: The sky isn't moving - you're standing on the part that is. Earth spins once every 24 hours, so every star appears to drift about 15 degrees per hour, sliding slowly out of a telescope's narrow view. A tracking mount points its axis at the North Celestial Pole and turns a motor the opposite way, exactly canceling that drift so a target holds still.
text_zh: 天空并没有在动——是你脚下的地球在转。地球每 24 小时自转一圈，所以每颗星星看起来每小时都会漂移大约 15 度，慢慢滑出望远镜狭窄的视野。跟踪支架把转轴对准北天极，用马达反向旋转，恰好抵消这种漂移，让目标保持静止。

title_en: The Real Cost of Higher Magnification
text_en: The same telescope, the same Jupiter: at 35x the image is small but bright and steady; at 80x it's larger but noticeably dimmer and shakier. Higher magnification spreads the same collected light over a bigger area and amplifies every bit of air turbulence and hand shake. More power is only better up to the point where the air and your gear can still support it.
text_zh: 同一台望远镜看同一个木星：35 倍时图像较小，却明亮稳定；80 倍时更大，也更暗、更抖。高倍率会把同样的光摊到更大面积，还会放大大气和支架的晃动。细节不再增加时，就该退回较低倍率。

text_en: Moons scar quietly: with no atmosphere to burn up incoming rocks, even small impactors punch straight through to the surface, splash debris outward, and leave a ring-shaped crater behind. Planets like Jupiter roil with weather on a giant scale - its cloud bands are layers of ammonia clouds, and its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth that has raged for centuries. Nebulae like Orion's are stellar nurseries: gravity slowly pulls a gas cloud inward until it collapses and ignites a brand-new star. And some stars end up enormous - Betelgeuse is so large that if it replaced the Sun, its surface would reach past Mars's orbit.
text_zh: 月球默默留下伤痕：没有大气层烧毁来袭的岩石，哪怕很小的撞击体也能直接砸到地表，把喷溅物甩向四周，留下一个环形的坑。像木星这样的行星有着巨大尺度的天气：它的条纹带是层层氨云，大红斑则是一场比地球还大、已经持续了几个世纪的风暴。像猎户座星云这样的星云是恒星的育婴房：引力慢慢把气体云拉拢，最终坍缩并点燃一颗全新的恒星。还有一些恒星大得惊人——参宿四如果取代太阳，它的表面会一直延伸到超过火星轨道的地方。

title_en: The Dobsonian: Big Mirror, Simple Box
title_zh: 多布森：大主镜，简单摇箱
text_en: John Dobson popularized large Newtonian tubes on simple rocker boxes and shared them through public sidewalk astronomy. Swivel for azimuth and tilt for altitude: the design makes big aperture accessible, but you provide the tracking with gentle hand nudges.
text_zh: 约翰·多布森推广了安装在简单摇箱上的大口径牛顿镜，并通过街头公众观测把它分享给更多人。左右旋转控制方位，上下俯仰控制高度：这种设计让大口径更亲民，但追踪要靠你轻柔地手动推镜。

title_en: The Cassegrain: A Folded Light Path
text_en: A two-mirror design published under Laurent Cassegrain's name in 1672 sends light from a concave primary to a convex secondary and back through the primary. Folding packs a long focal length into a short tube: high magnification, but a narrow field that rewards disciplined finder use.
text_zh: 1672 年以洛朗·卡塞格林之名发表的双镜设计，让光从凹面主镜到凸面副镜，再折返回主镜中央。这样能把长焦距装进短镜筒，不过主视野很窄，找目标时不能跳过寻星镜。

title_en: The Gregorian: Focus Before the Secondary
title_zh: 格里高利：先聚焦，再反射
text_en: In a Gregorian, light passes through a real focal point BEFORE reaching the concave secondary mirror. This gives an upright image, but the two curved mirrors and the mid-air focus must be aligned much more strictly than in a Newtonian.
text_zh: 在格里高利式中，光线先穿过一个真实的焦点，然后才到达凹面副镜。这带来正立的成像，但两面曲面镜和悬在半空的焦点必须比牛顿式对得更严格。

title_zh: 红外观测：从太空看见热
text_en: An infrared space telescope detects heat radiation instead of visible light. Infrared passes through dust that blocks visible light, revealing newborn stars - but the telescope must stay extremely cold behind its sunshield, or its own heat drowns the signal.
text_zh: 空间红外望远镜记录的是红外辐射，不是人眼看到的颜色。红外能穿过部分尘埃，显出其中的新生恒星；但望远镜必须躲在遮阳罩后保持低温，否则自身热量会盖住微弱信号。

title_en: Radio Astronomy: Data Instead of Images
title_zh: 射电天文：数据就是观测
text_en: FAST is a 500-meter radio telescope in Guizhou with an active reflector and a suspended feed cabin. It has no eyepiece: position the cabin, tune frequency, reject RFI, fold pulses, match dispersion measure, and integrate until SNR makes the hidden pattern credible. The trace IS the observation.
text_zh: FAST 是位于贵州的 500 米射电望远镜，使用主动反射面和悬吊馈源舱接收信号。它没有目镜：先稳住馈源舱，再调频、清除射频干扰、校正周期和色散量，最后持续积分。屏幕上的频谱和脉冲，就是这次观测留下的记录。

title_en: One Target, Many Kinds of Light
text_en: Visible light shows stars, infrared reveals warm dust, radio traces cold gas. No single instrument sees everything. Modern astronomy compares evidence from several wavelength windows and builds one conclusion supported by all of them.
text_zh: 可见光更容易显示恒星，红外能突出温暖尘埃，射电则能追踪冷气体。没有一台仪器能包办全部信息，把几个波段放在一起，天体的结构才会更清楚。

title_zh: 为什么用红外、为什么去太空
text_en: Earth's atmosphere protects life, but absorbs important infrared wavelengths; warm air and a warm telescope also glow in infrared. Modern observatories near places such as Sun-Earth L2 use distance, shielding, and deep cooling to protect faint infrared signals.
text_zh: 地球大气保护生命，却会吸收重要红外波段；温暖空气和温暖望远镜自身也会发出红外。现代观测站运行在日地 L2 等位置附近，利用距离、遮蔽和深度制冷保护暗弱红外信号。

text_en: JWST's 6.5 m primary mirror is 18 hexagonal beryllium segments coated in gold to reflect infrared well. It folds for launch, unfolds in space, and each segment is nudged by actuators until 18 star images merge into one - wavefront alignment.
text_zh: JWST 的 6.5 米主镜由 18 块六边形铍镜片组成，镀金以更好地反射红外。它折叠发射、在太空展开，每块镜片由执行器微调，直到 18 个星点合并成一个——这就是波前校准。

title_zh: 遮阳罩与 L2 轨道
text_en: Five sunshield layers block the heat of the Sun, Earth and Moon so the cold side reaches about 40 K (MIRI needs even colder). JWST sits near the Sun-Earth L2 point, ~1.5 million km from Earth, orbiting the SUN in a halo orbit - it does NOT orbit the Earth. There the Sun, Earth and Moon stay on one side, behind the shield.
text_zh: 五层遮阳罩挡住太阳、地球和月球的热量，使冷侧达到约 40K（MIRI 还需更冷）。JWST 位于日地 L2 点附近，距地球约 150 万公里，绕太阳做 halo 轨道运行——它不绕地球运行。在那里太阳、地球和月球始终在遮阳罩同一侧。

text_en: NIRCam images in the near infrared. NIRSpec takes spectra to read composition, motion and redshift. MIRI sees cold dust and molecules in the mid infrared but needs extra cooling. FGS/NIRISS guides precisely and adds niche near-infrared work. The right instrument depends on the science question.
text_zh: NIRCam 负责近红外成像；NIRSpec 用光谱测成分、运动和红移；MIRI 观察中红外的冷尘埃和分子，但需要额外制冷；FGS/NIRISS 负责精确导星和特定近红外观测。先看目标信息，再选对应仪器。

text_en: The detector records infrared photons, not eye colours. Each filter's data is mapped to red, green or blue to make a science image. Different colour mappings highlight dust, gas, temperature or star-forming regions. The final answer is a scientific interpretation, not just a pretty picture.
text_zh: 探测器记录的是不同红外波段的强度，不是人眼颜色。把各波段分别映射到红、绿、蓝后，尘埃、气体和恒星形成区会呈现不同结构。颜色要对应测量，不能只追求好看。

title_en: A Star Is a Point, Not a Disk
title_zh: 恒星是一个点，不是一个圆面
text_en: Stars are so far away that no telescope on Earth resolves their surfaces. All a star can ever be is a point. Out of focus, that point spreads into a soft round blob; as you reach the focal plane it collapses inward until it is as small and tight as your optics allow. So for a star, 'in focus' means smallest - not most detailed.
text_zh: 恒星实在太遥远了，地面上没有任何望远镜能分辨出它们的表面。恒星在望远镜里永远只能是一个点。失焦时，这个点会扩散成柔软的圆形光斑；当你接近焦平面时，它会不断向内收缩，直到达到光学系统允许的最小、最紧实的状态。所以对恒星来说，「合焦」意味着最小，而不是最多细节。

title_en: When a Narrow Field Is the Wrong Tool
title_zh: 窄视野反而是错误的工具
text_en: An open cluster like the Pleiades is over a degree wide - wider than a high-power eyepiece can show. Push the power up and you get a few bright stars with no shape, because the pattern that makes it a cluster has fallen outside the field. Some objects are identified by their overall shape, and for those the widest, lowest-power view is the correct one.
text_zh: 像昴星团这样的疏散星团展布超过一度，比高倍率目镜能呈现的范围还要宽。把倍率推高，你只会看到几颗没有形状可言的亮星，因为让它成为「星团」的那个整体图案已经落到视野之外了。有些目标是靠整体形状来辨认的，对它们来说，视野最宽、倍率最低的那一档才是正确答案。

text_en: Mars stays a small disk even in a large telescope, and its markings are only slightly darker than the ground around them. Magnification enlarges that faint difference but does not strengthen it - and it enlarges the air's turbulence at the same time. Low-contrast detail is won by precise focus, clean optics and steady air. Push the power too far and the markings wash out completely.
text_zh: 即使用大望远镜，火星也只是一个小圆面，而且它表面的暗纹只比周围略暗一点点。放大倍率只会把这一点微弱的差异放大，却不会让它变得更明显——与此同时，大气的扰动也被同样放大了。低对比度的细节靠的是精准调焦、干净的光学系统和平稳的大气。倍率推得太高，暗纹反而会被彻底冲淡。
